thread:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty INC-2026-089 triggered for service=runtime-serving, severity=sev2 — container crashloop on gpu-17 (k8s/node-gpu-17).

mike: seeing crashloop on runtime-engine pod runtime-zz-7f8b9. Crash reason: SIGSEGV in fused_kernels::execute +0x3a at fused_kernels.cu:142
Logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:22:01Z] runtime-engine[pid=1423]: cudaCheckError() failed: out of memory at fused_kernels.cu:140
[2026-03-15T14:22:01Z] runtime-engine[pid=1423]: terminating with signal SIGSEGV (11)
[2026-03-15T14:22:01Z] kernel: NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31, Traceback (cpu)=0x7f...
```

jin: thanks, grabbing on-call. quick kubectl: 
```
kubectl -n redwood get pods -o wide | grep runtime-zz
runtime-zz-7f8b9    0/1 CrashLoopBackOff   5 (1m ago)   32m   10.0.17.88   node-gpu-17
```

anita: is this isolated to node-gpu-17 or across cluster?

mike: currently only node-gpu-17. saw similar stack trace an hour ago on gpu-03 but that was a different model run; probably unrelated.

sara: @jin going to triage infra logs, looks like kubelet restarted on node-gpu-17 ~14:20 UTC (node-flap)? could be hardware flake.

infra-bot: node event: node-gpu-17 KubeletRestart reason=OOM_killer? count=1 timestamp=2026-03-15T14:20:12Z

leo: customer impact — Telemetry shows ~480 failed inferences in last 10m, 3 customers have errors (cust-A, cust-B, cust-C). cust-A is heavy traffic, ~60% of errors.

mike: mitigation plan: 1) cordon node-gpu-17 2) drain non-critical pods 3) scale down runtime daemonset on that node 4) restart runtime-engine after env tweak to disable fused kernels 5) collect core dump and upload.

jin: agree. doing cordon now.

ops-bot: command executed by jin: `kubectl cordon node-gpu-17` — success

jin: draining runtime pods off node (graceful). Running: `kubectl drain node-gpu-17 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force`

mike: while drain runs — set env var MODEL_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED_KERNELS=1 in runtime deployment and roll the pods. This will force the runtime to use safe kernels (slower but stable).

anita: do we have safe fallback for TensorRT fused path? For some models we use TRT kernels; disabling might increase latency but should avoid segfault.

mike: yes, fallback to cuBLAS/cuDNN code path when fused disabled. expect ~1.4x token latency for heavy seq lengths.

leo: alerting customers: starting template notice to affected customers. I'll escalate cust-A to SEs.

infra-bot: drain completed; runtime pods rescheduled to node-gpu-05 and node-gpu-08. Pod runtime-zz-7f8b9 terminated.

mike: rolling update to runtime config; applying patch: 
```
kubectl -n redwood set env deployment/runtime-runtime MODEL_RUNTIME_DISABLE_FUSED_KERNELS=1
kubectl rollout restart deployment/runtime-runtime
```

sara: copying kernel logs and dmesg from node-gpu-17 to /tmp for upload. Some NV GPU errors show: `NVRM: GPU at 65:00: Illegal memory access` right before SIGSEGV.

mike: confirmed restart finished, new runtime pods in Running state on gpu-05/gpu-08. Monitoring.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-2026-089 assigned to jin (on-call). Priority: P1 -> P2 after mitigations.

jin: quick QA — firing synthetic request against affected model to replicate: got success on new pod, previously failed.

mike: good. keeping node-gpu-17 cordoned. Next steps: 1) extract core dump and /var/log/nvidia* 2) collect container logs and stacktrace 3) open bug and upload to S3 (s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-089/) 4) plan a kernel-driver repro on isolated hardware if needed.

anita: will triage model version used on gpu-17 — sending model metadata.

leo: customer communication: sent initial "we are mitigating" message to cust-A/B/C. ETA: 30m for full verification.

mike: note — runtime pods used a quantized model variant with custom fused-kernel optimization (experimental). I'm tagging that variant as suspect.

jin: collecting metrics — token latency up 20% cluster-wide due to fallback kernels. Spike aligns with rollout time.

ops-bot: recorded action: cordon node-gpu-17, disabled fused kernels, rolled runtime, collected logs.

mike: uploading logs now: `tar czf /tmp/INC-2026-089-logs.tgz /var/log/runtime /var/log/nvidia* /tmp/core.*` then `aws s3 cp /tmp/INC-2026-089-logs.tgz s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2026-089/`

infra-bot: upload complete. bug filed: RW-ISSUE-4523 — title: SIGSEGV in fused_kernels on node-gpu-17; labels=sev2, runtime, fused-kernels, customer-impact.

sara: quick note — node-gpu-17 shows ECC errors earlier in day; ops should tag hardware for out-of-band check.

jin: handoff — I'll stay on follow-up until next shift @ 18:00 UTC. If anything regresses ping me.

mike: post-incident actions: 1) disable experimental fused kernels by default for all prod until we ship verified kernels 2) add preflight checks for ECC/GPU health before scheduling heavy quantized workloads 3) add per-node telemetry for NVRM Xid errors and auto-cordon thresholds.

leo: I logged customer follow-up tasks in the incident runbook and CC'd SEs.

anita: labeling the offending model variant and creating rollback plan — rolling back variants for cust-A so they don't hit experimental path during peak.

pagerduty-bot: INC-2026-089 status update: mitigated — service degraded, not fully recovered. Incident lead: jin. Impact: transient errors for 3 customers, ~480 failed inferences.

mike: closing notes for the thread: keep node-gpu-17 cordoned until HW validated. Do not re-enable fused kernels until we have a repro and test coverage.

leo: marking cust-A priority follow-up.

jin: thanks all — I'll file the detailed postmortem with timelines and attach the S3 logs.

mike: :thumbsup: good job.
